content: Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) encompasses a range of liver conditions, starting from simple hepatic steatosis (fat accumulation in the liver) to more advanced stages, such as Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis (NASH) and cirrhosis. In severe cases, this progression can result in hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer). NAFLD is particularly common in individuals with type 2 diabetes, with a significant prevalence observed in this population. NASH, which represents the progressive and more severe form of NAFLD, has emerged as one of the leading indications for liver transplantation globally. Management of NAFLD in patients with diabetes necessitates the implementation of specific, targeted therapeutic strategies. This is due to the strong association of NAFLD with increased cardiovascular and metabolic risks in this population.
